name: Mental Maths: 3-Digit × 3-Digit Multiplication — Structure & Strategy
description: A KaTeX-enabled advanced deck for structured three-digit multiplication. It distinguishes genuinely mental-friendly cases from arbitrary calculations, covering core chunking, friendly factors, near-1000 methods, difference of squares, estimates, limitations, and error checks.
estimatedTime: 180–230 minutes for a first focused pass; then 10–20 minute review bursts

cards.term: 3-Digit × 3-Digit: What is the honest goal of mental methods here?
cards.definition:
Not every three-digit by three-digit product should be done wholly in the head. This deck teaches the structured cases that genuinely reduce effort: friendly factors, nearby bases, balanced products, and one-factor chunking.

For arbitrary numbers, written working is often the best method.

cards.term: 3-Digit × 3-Digit: What is the safest core method?
cards.definition:
Split one factor into hundreds, tens, and ones.

$$
\begin{aligned}
236\times124 \\
&=236\times100+236\times20+236\times4 \\
&=23600+4720+944 \\
&=29264
\end{aligned}
$$

When one factor is near 100, 200, 500, or 1000.

$$
\begin{aligned}
384\times199 \\
&=384\times200-384 \\
&=76800-384 \\
&=76416
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: 3-Digit × 3-Digit: When does a factor of 125 help?
cards.definition:
When the other factor has an 8.

$$
\begin{aligned}
768\times125 \\
&=96\times1000 \\
&=96000
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: 3-Digit × 3-Digit: When does a factor of 625 help?
cards.definition:
Because 625 × 16 = 10000.

$$
\begin{aligned}
625\times128 \\
&=8\times10000 \\
&=80000
\end{aligned}
$$

For values close to 1000, cross-subtract or cross-add, and use a 3-digit right part.

$$
\begin{aligned}
997\times996 \\
997-4&=993 \\
3\times4&=012 \\
997\times996&=993012
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: 3-Digit × 3-Digit: Why must the right part have three digits near 1000?
cards.definition: Because the base is 1000. For 998 × 997, the right part is 2 × 3 = 006, giving 995006, not 9956.

Use difference of squares for equally spaced factors.

$$
\begin{aligned}
498\times502 \\
&=500^2-2^2 \\
&=250000-4 \\
&=249996
\end{aligned}
$$

Round to convenient hundreds.

486 × 312 ≈ 500 × 300 = 150000. The exact product should be around that size.

cards.term: 3-Digit × 3-Digit: When should you stop using mental-only methods?
cards.definition: When the calculation has no friendly structure and maintaining several large partial products risks mistakes. Use paper or a calculator; choosing the right tool is good numeracy.

Near-1000, both below.

$$
\begin{aligned}
997-4&=993 \\
3\times4&=012 \\
997\times996&=993012
\end{aligned}
$$

Difference of squares around 500.

$$
\begin{aligned}
498\times502 \\
&=500^2-2^2 \\
&=249996

$$

Core one-factor chunking.

$$
\begin{aligned}
236\times124 \\
&=236\times100+236\times20+236\times4 \\
&=23600+4720+944 \\
&=29264
\end{aligned}
$$
Use an estimate and last-digit check. 236 × 124 ≈ 200 × 100 = 20000, and 6 × 4 = 24, so the result ends in 4. Exact result: 29264.
